subject: Containment tiering, response windows & commit-discount proposal
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie@starlight.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question: containment tiers + committed discount

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Starlight is excited about Redwood's runtime economics. Procurement asked me to get a concrete proposal for SLA packaging we can take to our CFO. High level ask: a pricing/packaging slide for (a) 99.9% vs 99.95% uptime bands, (b) response windows for Priority 1 / P2 incidents (options: 1h, 2h, 4h), and (c) escalation coverage (business hours vs 24x7 on-call + an on-call retainer model).

Couple of constraints from our side: we can commit to a 12-month consumption baseline if we get meaningful unit discounts and a softened incident credit calculation for transient platform-level token spikes (we run batch workloads overnight). Also need to understand what a pilot (30-day PO/waiver) would look like.

Can you send a short proposal and a simple mutual action plan (dates, technical POC, procurement steps)? If possible, include any optional add-on pricing for a dedicated on-call retainer and a reduced penalty ladder for the first 60 days of the contract.

Thanks — cc'ing our procurement mailbox: procurement@starlight.ai

—Jamie
Jamie Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, Starlight AI
jamie@starlight.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Packaging question: containment tiers + committed discount

Team — forwarding Jamie's ask. Quick guidance needed:
- Feasibility: 1-hour response for P1 across a 24x7 escalation (with on-call retainer) — ops impact?
- Pricing input: what banded discounts do we typically give for a 12-month committed baseline vs pay-as-you-go? Starlight indicated overnight batch spikes — how do we treat transient token spikes in credit calculations?
- Legal: is there wiggle room to soften penalty ladder for first 60 days for pilot customers?

Goal: get a concrete one-pager and a shallow pricing matrix we can send back today. I can own the external reply.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0124

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: containment tiers + committed discount

Marissa / Naomi —
Quick notes from infra/finance POV. I've mocked a pricing matrix (attached) but listing key tradeoffs here:

1) Uptime bands (per-month SLA credit basis):
   - 99.9% (3.65 hours/month downtime): baseline unit price
   - 99.95% (1.82 hours/month downtime): +12% premium to baseline
   - 99.99% (0.44 hours/month downtime): +30% premium and requires reserved capacity pool for guaranteed throughput

2) Response windows / Escalation:
   - P1: 1-hour response (followed by triage & mitigation plan) requires dedicated on-call retainer (recommended $8,000/mo) or a higher commit threshold; ops headcount impact significant for sustained P1 volume.
   - P1: 2-hour response feasible without retainer for most accounts — we can absorb with current rotation.
   - P2: 4-hour response standard.

3) Transient token spike handling:
   - For batch/spike patterns we can bucket consumption by 24-hour rolling window for the first 90 days. If average consumption over the baseline period stays within committed corridor, we will not levy incident credits for token spikes below X% of baseline. Need legal to define X (we usually use 150% as guardrail for the pilot).

4) Commit discounts (12-month baseline): tiered by committed spend: 
   - >= $250k ARR equivalent: 15% unit discount
   - >= $500k: 22% unit discount + waived onboarding fee
   - >= $1M: 30% unit discount + 1-month pilot credit + discounted retainer (25% off)

5) Penalty ladder softening for pilot: we can offer a 60-day limited exposure window where penalty caps at 50% of normal SLA credit. Full SLA credit ladder applies after day 61.

Attached: pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx (quick numbers), sample wording for pilot clause.

If you want to push for 1-hour P1 without retainer, we should price the premium into the unit rate — it's expensive to staff.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie@starlight.ai>, procurement@starlight.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Rapid containment & response tiers + 12-month commit economics (summary)

Hi Jamie / Procurement —
Thanks — attached is a concise proposal we discussed. Summary below so you can circulate:

What we propose (high level)
- Uptime options: 99.9% (baseline) | 99.95% (+12% unit premium) | 99.99% (+30%, reserved pool)
- Response windows (per-incident SLA categorization):
   * Priority 1 (platform-down/severe degradation): 1 hour (with $8K/mo retainer) or 2 hours (without retainer)
   * Priority 2 (partial degradation): 4 hours standard
- Escalation coverage: 24x7 on-call available as an add-on (retainer pricing above) or business-hours only for baseline packages
- Pilot: 30-day pilot available; 60-day limited-exposure SLA credit cap (50% of normal credits) if you opt into the pilot; for >= $1M commit we provide 1-month pilot credit

Economics snapshot (examples)
- 12-month commit bands: 15% / 22% / 30% discounts at $250k / $500k / $1M thresholds respectively (see attached commit_pricing_sheet.xlsx for worked examples)
- Retainer option: $8,000/mo (standard) — discounted to $6,000/mo at $1M commit

Next steps
1) Confirm which uptime band and response window you prefer (99.95% with 2-hour vs 99.95% with 1-hour + retainer?).
2) Schedule a 45-min call with our infra lead to align on pilot scope (I suggest Wed 22 Apr 10:00 PT).
3) I'll share an SLA addendum draft and a DocuSign link for a non-binding MSA amendment for review.

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_Redwood_v1.pdf, commit_pricing_sheet.xlsx
DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/REDWOOD-STL-STANDARD-SLA

If you want, we can carve a specific clause to exclude brief scheduled batch windows from credit calculations for the first 90 days — Karthik's team recommended a 24-hour rolling bucket with a 150% guardrail.

Appreciate the quick review — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Liu <jamie@starlight.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@starlight.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Rapid containment & response tiers + 12-month commit economics (summary)

Marissa —
Thanks for the clear breakdown and for the pilot flexibility. We like the 99.95% band with the 2-hour P1 response for now (avoids retainer until we see production). A couple of asks before we circulate to legal & finance:

- Can you soften the penalty calculation to explicitly exclude scheduled nightly batch windows for the first 60 days (rather than 'soften' credits overall)? That helps our teams avoid false positives during ramp.
- For the pilot waiver/credit: would you be able to confirm a 1-month credit in writing if we hit >= $1M commit at signature? Jamie (cc'd procurement) — procurement will confirm the PO cadence.

If those two items are in writing we can move quickly — please send the updated addendum and we'll route internally.
